School vocabulary
Start up
Set up a new business — Montar / crear.
They started up a bakery last year.
School vocabulary
Pay back
Do something bad to someone in revenge — Devolvérsela a / vengarse de.
He paid them back for the insult.
School vocabulary
Pay off
Bribe someone — Sobornar / untar.
The inspector had been paid off.
Turn out to be worth the effort — Dar fruto / merecer la pena.
All that studying paid off.
School vocabulary
Hand over
Give someone responsibility for something — Ceder / traspasar.
She handed over the project to her deputy.
School vocabulary
Take back
Admit that what you said was wrong — Retirar / retractarse de.
I take back what I said about him.
Remind someone of the past — Transportar a / traer recuerdos.
That smell takes me back to childhood.
School vocabulary
Line up
Arrange for someone or something to be available — Organizar / conseguir.
We've lined up a guitarist for the party.
Put things straight with one another — Alinear / cuadrar.
Line the edges up before you glue them.
School vocabulary
Give away
Reveal a secret by accident — Delatar / dejar escapar.
His face gave the secret away.
School vocabulary
Work out
Turn out a certain way — Salir / resultar.
Everything worked out in the end.
Calculate or solve something — Calcular / resolver.
Work out the total before you pay.
School vocabulary
Warm up
Make something warmer — Calentar.
Warm up the soup for me.
Let a machine run briefly before using it — Dejar calentar / precalentar.
Warm the engine up first.
School vocabulary
Stick to
Stay attached to something — Pegarse a / adherirse a.
The rice stuck to the pan.
Keep to one subject — Ceñirse a / limitarse a.
Please stick to the question.
School vocabulary
Get over
Stop being upset about something — Superar / olvidar.
It took her a year to get over it.
School vocabulary
Wear out
Become damaged or weak from use — Desgastarse / gastarse.
These shoes wear out quickly.
School vocabulary
Keep off
Not walk or stand on something — No pisar.
Keep off the grass.
School vocabulary
Grow up
Stop behaving childishly — Madurar / dejar de hacer el niño.
Oh, grow up and apologise.
School vocabulary
Eat up
Use up all of something, such as time or money — Consumir / comerse.
The repairs ate up our savings.
School vocabulary
Fix up
Make yourself look smart — Arreglarse.
She fixed herself up for the party.
Arrange for someone to have something — Apañar / conseguirle a alguien.
The agent fixed us up with a car.
School vocabulary
Get together
Collect things into one place — Reunir / juntar.
Get your papers together before we go.
Regain control of yourself — Recomponerse / centrarse.
He needs to get himself together.
School vocabulary
Leave behind
Go ahead of others who cannot keep up — Dejar atrás / adelantar.
She left the rest of the class behind.
School vocabulary
Settle down
Become calmer or quieter — Calmarse / tranquilizarse.
The children settled down after lunch.
Become less confused or violent — Apaciguarse / normalizarse.
The situation settled down by evening.
School vocabulary
Take in
Be tricked by someone — Dejarse engañar por.
We were completely taken in by him.
Make a piece of clothing smaller — Meter / estrechar.
The tailor took the jacket in.
School vocabulary
Grow out of
Become too big for clothes — Quedársele pequeño a uno.
He has grown out of his coat.
School vocabulary
Take over
Take control of a place by force — Tomar / apoderarse de.
Rebels took over the radio station.
Start doing a job someone else was doing — Relevar / sustituir.
I'll take over while you rest.
School vocabulary
Calm down
Become less confused or violent — Apaciguarse / serenarse.
Things calmed down after the police arrived.
